items.title: The Risk of Russian Sabotage in Europe: A Fight That Spirals Out of Control

items.title: Families Turn to Symbolic Cremation After Nepal Floods
items.summary: Thousands are missing, and some families have lost hope of recovering their bodies. To carry out his sacred duty, a son lights the funeral pyre for a straw effigy of his father.

items.title: Alejandro Betancourt, Trump’s Partner in Venezuelan Oil Deal, Has Faced Investigations

items.title: Germany’s Far Right, Edging Close to Power, Remains Close to Extremists
items.summary: The Alternative for Germany party has tried to soften its hard-line image but is still privately working with extremists. It could win a state election on Sunday.

items.title: Russian Drone Strikes Office of Ukraine’s Intelligence Chief
items.summary: The attack came as the American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were said to be planning imminent visits to Kyiv and to Moscow.

items.title: Inside the Nepal Tunnel Rescue Operation

items.title: Yemen’s Houthis Push Toward Red Sea Strait as Ground Fighting Escalates
items.summary: The Houthis, an Iran-backed militia, appear to be trying to gain control of a port city near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key choke point for global trade.

items.title: U.A.E. Pardons Egyptian Dissident Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison
items.summary: Abdulrahman al-Qaradawi was extradited from Lebanon to the Emirates, a close U.S. ally, after criticizing its government, in a case that alarmed human rights experts.

items.title: Israel Says It Is Cementing Its Foothold in Southern Lebanon
items.summary: The recent capture of a strategic ridge has further entrenched the Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory, as efforts to broker lasting peace have floundered.

items.title: Philippines’ Vice President Faces Arrest Over Assassination Threats

items.title: The U.S. Wants the Oil From These 17 Venezuelan Fields
items.summary: A private oil company has struck a deal with the Trump administration to develop 17 areas in Venezuela, an effort that experts say will take years and billions of dollars.

items.title: How Gloria Steinem and Ms. Magazine Transformed the Publishing Industry
items.summary: The late feminist icon insisted that women were not a niche audience — and proved it in 1971 with the start of an influential publication owned and operated by them.

items.title: Tesla’s Cybercab Is Being Investigated by Federal Regulators

items.title: The Pros and Cons of Paying Off Your Mortgage Early

items.summary: Researchers investigating how OpenAI’s A.I. agents were able to break into Hugging Face’s infrastructure weren’t allowed to look at the incident’s full scope.

items.summary: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.

items.title: Noise and Motion Monitors in Their Homes? These Tenants Say No.

items.title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
items.summary: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.
